page.layout: One page of text, two sections. Running head at top: "VANITATE." with page number 107 at upper right. Below it a heading line "VIII. GAL." Then a French poem of 7 lines with a large initial M, followed by a centred heading "LAT." and a Latin poem of verse lines in italic. No margin notes.

main_text.head: VIII. GAL.
main_text.p: MONDAIN, si tu le sais, di moy, quel est le Monde?
main_text.l: S'il est bon, pourquoy doc tant de mal y abode?
S'il est mauuais, pourquoy le vas tu tant cerchant?
S'il est doux, comment donc a il tant d'amertume?
S'il est amer, comment te va il allechant?
S'il est ami, pourquoy a il ceste coustume
De tuer l'homme vain, sous ses pieds abatu?
Et s'il est ennemi, pourquoy t'y fies tu?
main_text.head: LAT.

l.i: Qua causa melle ut dulcius id putet,

page.notes: The French and Latin lines are transcribed as printed. The initial M of the French poem is a large decorated capital. The Latin "Quae" in the last line has a superscript mark over the final letters ("Quaeʒ") that I could not fully confirm; the reading "Quae" is uncertain. The word "tant" in line 3 and "sçais" spelling are read as printed ("sais"). Line 1 "Mondain" is the opening word set in small capitals. Some letters in the French lines are faint and "doc" (line 2) and "abode" could be "doc"/"abode" with a bar over the o; read as printed.
